children: The broader market indices, Nifty Smallcap 100 and Nifty Midcap 100, fell up to 3 percent on Friday, extending their losing streak to a seventh consecutive session and underperforming the benchmark Nifty, which declined 1 percent.
The Nifty gave up its early gains to extend losses for a fourth straight session amid rising oil prices and tensions in West Asia.
The Nifty Smallcap 100 fell 3.63 percent to hit a low of 17,611.40. The index has declined around 8 percent over the past seven sessions.

As many as 96 of the index's 100 constituents were trading in the red. TD Power Systems was the biggest laggard, falling more than 8 percent. Urban Company, Inox Wind, Ola Electric Mobility and Karur Vysya Bank followed, declining up to 7 percent.

The Nifty Midcap 100 also remained under pressure, falling 2.73 percent to a low of 55,501.15. The index extended its losing streak to seven consecutive sessions, shedding around 7 percent during the period.
Only four of its 100 constituents traded in positive territory, while the remaining 96 were in the red. Swiggy led the losses, plunging 16 percent following its quarterly results.

The decline came after the food delivery company reported wider losses in its quick-commerce business during the September quarter of the 2026-27 financial year, keeping the focus on profitability in the competitive segment. The results followed those of rival Eternal earlier this week.
Several brokerages also cut their target prices for Swiggy, citing concerns over its quick-commerce execution, profitability and competitive position.
Motilal Oswal Financial Services, National Aluminium Company, Adani Total Gas and Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services were among the other major midcap laggards, falling up to 5 percent.

title: Broader markets crash up to 3%, extend decline to 7th straight session: What lies ahead?
